faq.q: Where does the water go when clothes dry?
faq.a: The water evaporates: it turns into water vapour, an invisible gas, and mixes into the air. Later it may help form clouds and fall again as rain.
Evaporation is when a liquid slowly turns into a gas at its surface, without boiling. Puddles, wet clothes and sweat all dry by evaporation.

faq.q: Why do clothes dry faster in the wind?
faq.a: Wind carries away the damp air right next to the clothes and brings in drier air, so water can keep escaping quickly.

faq.q: Why do clothes dry faster in the sun?
faq.a: Heat gives the water particles more energy, so more of them escape into the air each second.

faq.q: Why should clothes be spread out to dry?
faq.a: Spreading clothes out gives a bigger surface touching the air, so more water can evaporate at once. A scrunched-up shirt dries slowly in the middle.
asks: Why does a folded towel stay wet?

facts: Evaporation happens at the surface of a liquid at temperatures below its boiling point.
Warmth, wind, low humidity and a large surface area all speed up evaporation.

quiz.say: When wet clothes dry, what happens to the water?
quiz.why: The water evaporates into water vapour, an invisible gas in the air.

wrong.1: Water never vanishes; it becomes vapour in the air.
wrong.2: The washing line stays dry; the water goes into the air.

quiz.say: Which day will dry the washing fastest?
quiz.why: Warmth speeds up evaporation and wind carries the damp air away.

wrong.0: Cold, still air dries clothes slowly.
wrong.2: Fog means the air is already damp, so drying is very slow.
